# Control robustness does not make internal processing free

Status: root cost note, independent review pending. Mathematical path-law action, not a hardware work certificate.

For the actual admitted overdamped model with diffusion matrix 2 beta^(-1)D (constant SPD D), reference drift b, and additional predetermined drift s(t)c(x), the compact smooth transverse construction makes c bounded. On every finite horizon s is locally essentially bounded, hence the Girsanov exponential satisfies Novikov's criterion. With the SAME initial law, controlled and reference un-killed trajectory laws have

 KL(P_controlled[0,T] || P_reference[0,T])
 = (beta/4) E_controlled integral_0^T s(t)^2 c(X_t)^T D^(-1)c(X_t)dt.

This is the standard Brownian change-of-drift action. For stationary initialization pi, received common invariance makes it exactly

 (beta/4) [integral_0^T s(t)^2dt] [integral c^T D^(-1)c d pi].

For conditional-basin initialization the expectation remains explicit and can be upper bounded by the maximum spatial quadratic norm times integral s^2. Stopping/recording at a killed boundary is a measurable data reduction, so the stopped-record relative entropy is no larger; do not assert equality for an arbitrary discarded/censored record.

Thus an amplitude-independent clock-error theorem is compatible with arbitrarily large control action and increasingly distinguishable full trajectories. The invariant measure or potential-energy neutrality does NOT mean zero apparatus power, zero entropy production, free switching, or a physically acquired controller. Translating this mathematical action into joules, force-generator limitations, calibration, bandwidth or noise requires an actual physical device model. None is supplied here.

# Strict mean increase needs only a short FIXED-amplitude pulse

This strengthens and simplifies the finite-rate limit argument in
TIME_DEPENDENT_MIXING_CAN_STRICTLY_INCREASE_MEAN.md (SHA-256
c6d797b8a9a8d6ac9ca9ed4bff8afa52a9d0f4120cb291bcca8bd71874361484).
All its definitions A,C,m,v and u(t) are unchanged. Select a sufficiently
small positive calendar time t so that u_1(t)>u_0(t).

Fix ANY finite R>0, for example R=1. Apply A+RC for duration epsilon starting
at t, and A otherwise. Let J(epsilon) be total mean lifetime from m. Exact
splitting of the occupation integral gives

    J(epsilon)=int_0^t <1,u(s)>_m ds
      +int_0^epsilon <1,exp[-s(A+RC)]u(t)>_m ds
      +<v,exp[-epsilon(A+RC)]u(t)>_m.

Finite-dimensional differentiation at epsilon=0, together with Av=1, gives

    J'(0)=<1,u(t)>_m-<v,(A+RC)u(t)>_m
         =-R<v,Cu(t)>_m
         =R(v_0-v_1)(u_1(t)-u_0(t))/3>0.

Thus J(epsilon)>J(0)=Q for all sufficiently small positive epsilon. The pulse
amplitude R remains FIXED and finite; no arbitrarily strong processing,
instantaneous permutation, intervention limit, source observation, or state
feedback is needed. The reference killed chain and full reference Q also stay
fixed. The extra form RC is nonnegative, reversible, common-measure preserving,
and annihilates h=1_D on both sides at every time.

This is a strict-increase boundary, not an unbounded-ratio counterexample.
The nonautonomous constant-four principle and sharp near-clock limit remain
unchallenged. The rare-gadget near-clock embedding described in README.md
scales this positive first variation by eta and preserves all receiving.

# Optional boundary audit: path-law action and a strict mean-increase pulse

Date: 2026-11-01 UTC. These are separate boundary receipts. They do not change
the independently accepted common-form/sharp-mean receipt or either prior ZIP.

## 1. Girsanov action note — PASS with a precise KL reading

Frozen source `neutral_processing_clock_pending_20261101/PROCESSING_ACTION_COST_ROOT.md`,
SHA-256 `d81b0f3f869d3652407455a7374373d89c82687442cab8953542ad37e4f691ea`.

For the actually received nonexplosive diffusion with constant noise covariance
2 beta^-1 D, D SPD, let Sigma Sigma^T=2 beta^-1 D. The added drift is
s(t)c(x), with c smooth compactly supported and bounded and s predetermined and
locally essentially bounded. The Brownian change-of-drift vector is

  theta=Sigma^-1 s(t)c(X_t),
  ||theta||^2=(beta/2)s(t)^2 c(X_t)^T D^-1 c(X_t).

On every finite horizon its integrated square is bounded by a deterministic
finite constant. Thus Novikov holds under either process and the stochastic
integrals needed to take the controlled expectation have mean zero. With the
SAME initial law, the path-law relative entropy is exactly

  KL(P_controlled[0,T] || P_reference[0,T])
    =(1/2)E_controlled int_0^T ||theta||^2dt
    =(beta/4)E_controlled int_0^T s(t)^2 c^T D^-1 c(X_t)dt.

This statement uses actual nonexplosion, uniqueness/identification of the drift-
changed SDE, constant nondegenerate diffusion and the finite-horizon Novikov
bound; it is not inferred just from a formal generator.

If the common invariant probability pi is the actual initial law, then every
controlled-time marginal is pi. Tonelli yields precisely the factorization
in the source. For a nonzero field in L2(pi), scaling a fixed nonzero schedule
by amplitude A makes this path-law KL grow as A^2. For a conditional-basin
start, the stated spatial-supremum upper bound remains valid, but the stationary
factorization need not hold.

**Controlling interpretation:** “increasingly distinguishable” is supported here
as growth of this path-law RELATIVE ENTROPY. Large KL alone does not establish
TV tending to one or vanishing optimal testing error. In fact a compact-field
example may retain a positive-probability set of finite-horizon trajectories
that never visit its support and are unaffected by amplitude. No stronger TV
limit is needed for the note's intended no-free-control point.
